The Police Sub-Inspector of Rajarajeshwari Nagara Police Station, Bengaluru has filed Police Report against the above named accused alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. The Prosecution case in brief is that on 30.04.2007, the marriage of the accused was solemnized with CW1 and after their marriage, they were residing together House No.20, 4 th Cross, Subbanna Garden, Bengaluru within the territorial jurisdiction of Rajarajeshwari Nagara Police Station.
One week after the marriage, the accused quarreled with CW1 demanding her to transfer BDA site standing in the name of her mother to his name and sent her to the house of CW4.
Since, the accused has not taken CW1 even after 2 months, on 28.06.2007, CW4 executed Gift Deed in respect of the said site to the name of CW1.
As the said Gift Deed was not executed in his name, on the same day he quarreled with CW1.
For the said reason, CW1 registered half portion of the said site to the name of the accused.
Thereafter, the accused took CW1 to his house.

After he took CW1 to his house,
he started to suspect on CW1; if he speaks with anybody, he was linking relationship with them; if she went to bring vegetables, he was linking relationship with the vegetable shop keeper; he was harassing CW1 stating that in his dream, some one was with her; he was defaming her if she went to her parent's house; he was harassing CW1 daily demanding money of Rs.2.00 Crores to bring from her parent's house stating that if she want to live happily, she should bring money otherwise, he will not allow her to live peacefully; abusing her in filthy languages and gave life threat stating that if she is not bring money, he will finish her.
Thereby, the accused has committed the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code .
3. Based on the First Information of CW1, the crime was registered in Crime No.330/2020 at Rajarajeshwari Nagara Police Station.
During investigation, the accused appeared before this Court and enlarged on bail.

On completion of the investigation, the Police Sub-Inspector of Rajarajeshwari Nagara Police Station, Bengaluru City filed Police Report against the accused alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code.

sentences.text: After taking cognizance of the said offences, the process was issued to the accused.
He has appeared before this Court.
The copies of the Police Report and other prosecution papers are furnished to the accused under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing, since there were grounds for presuming that the accused has committed offences triable by this Court, charges for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code has been framed and read over to the accused in Kannada language.
He has pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
4. To prove the charges framed against the accused, the prosecution has produced the oral evidences of PW1 and the documentary evidences in Ex.P1 and Ex.P2.

Since, there were no incriminating circumstances appearing in the evidences of the prosecution witnesses against the accused, the Station vs Perused The Materials Available On ... on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173485860/
2 examination of the accused under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. was dispensed with.
Heard the arguments of learned Senior Assistant Public Prosecutor and the learned counsel for the accused.
Perused the materials available on record.

5. The points for determination are;
1. Whether prosecution has proved the offences charged against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code beyond reasonable doubt?
2. What order or sentence?
6.

My answers to the above points are as follows:
 Point No.1 : In the Negative
PW1 Smt.S.Soumya is the First Informant, Mahazar witness and the injured.
The prosecution has also produced the documentary evidences Ex.P1 and Ex.P2.
Among them, Ex.P1 is the First Information and Ex.P2 is the Spot Mahazar.

8. As per the case of the prosecution, based on Ex.P1 given by PW1, the crime has been registered in Crime No.330/2020 and on investigation, since, there are evidences collected by the Investigation Officer to prosecute the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, the Police Report was filed.
In the First Information - Ex.P1, there are statements of PW1 with regard to the alleged incident committed by the accused.

PW1 in her examination-in-chief has deposed that on 30.04.2007, her marriage was solemnized with the accused and after their marriage, she was living with the accused at House No.20, 4 th Cross,
Subbanna Garden, Bengaluru.

She has also deposed in her examination-in-chief that the accused has not given any physical or mental harassment to her; no quarrel was taken place between her and the accused; since there were some petty differences between her and the accused, she gave First Information as per Ex.P1; she does not know its contents; she does not know the contents of Ex.P2;
she signed the said document at Police Station and; the Police have not conducted any Mahazar in her presence and she and the accused are residing together.
She has been considered as hostile witness and cross-examined at the request of the prosecution.
During cross-examination, she has denied the contents of Ex.P1; she gave it and the mahazar conducted at the place of incident as per Ex.P2 in her presence.
Nothing has been elicited in her cross- examination supporting the case of the prosecution.
She has admitted that she compromised the matter with the accused.
9. On perusal of the above evidences of PW1, it appears that the First Informant and the injured witnesses PW1 has deposed not supporting the case of the prosecution.

She has deposed in her Station vs Perused The Materials Available On ... on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173485860/
3 cross-examination that she and the accused has compromised the matter.
She has deposed in her examination-in-chief that she is residing with the accused.
Therefore, if the evidences of the other prosecution witnesses are recorded, no purpose will be served.
For this reason, the evidences of CW2 to CW10 are dropped.

Under these circumstances, I am holding that the prosecution has not proved the guilt of the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code beyond all reasonable doubt.
Hence, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.

10. POINT No.2 :- For the reasons stated in Point No.1, the prosecution has not proved the guilt of the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code beyond all reasonable doubt.
Therefore, the accused is not found guilty for the aforesaid offences charged against him.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following;
 ORDERS
Under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C, the  accused is hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code.
His bail bond and surety bond executed under Section 437 of Cr.P.C. will be in force till completion of appeal period and thereafter, it will be stand canceled.
(Typed by the Stenographer in the Court Computer on my direct dictation, printout taken, corrected and then pronounced by me in the open court on 19.04.2023)
(VEDAMOORTHY B.S.) II Addl.
